title: Boiled Potato, fresh, peel not eaten, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Boiled potato is a cooked tuber of the potato plant (Solanum tuberosum) prepared without added fat. The peel is not consumed, while the flesh retains most of the nutrients. Potato is a major source of carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals in many diets worldwide.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes were introduced to Europe from South America in the 16th century.
There are over 4,000 potato varieties differing in colour, shape, and taste.
Boiling preserves a large portion of vitamin C if the potatoes are not left in cold water for too long.
The peel contains more fiber and some vitamins, but it is omitted in this product.
Potato is one of the most widely consumed root vegetables in the world.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Boiled potato provides slow‑releasing energy, which helps maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C acts as an antioxidant, supports the immune system, and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart and muscle function.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Even without the peel, the flesh contains some fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes this product suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: Improperly stored or sprouted potatoes may contain solanine, a toxin that can cause nausea and headaches.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Boiled potatoes have a high glycemic index, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: Potential contamination
items.content: Improper handling can lead to bacterial growth and foodborne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled potatoes can be eaten plain, added to salads, soups, mashed, or used as a filling. They can be sliced, cubed, or pureed. When serving, you may garnish with fresh herbs, spices, or a drizzle of olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store boiled potatoes in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 3–4 days. Allow them to cool completely before refrigerating. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags.
